item: mols39-ext1 (cheap distinct target path suggested by parent): G6-equivariant seventh row for the exact Sage DM_39_6_1
proof_sketch: Let C be the exact column set of D (6 x 39, G6-invariant exactly). A new row f with f(g.c) = mu_g f(c) for all g in G6 is determined by its values on orbit representatives, restricted on each orbit to w with (mu_h - 1) w = 0 for h in Stab(c). The 7-row array [D; f] is a DM iff for every old row i the 39 values D_i(c) - f(c) are distinct (pairs among old rows are already fine). Grouping columns by orbit, this is exactly an exact cover: items (i, value) for the 6 old rows and 39 values, plus one item per orbit; option (orbit, w) covers its 6 x |orbit| items (options with an internal repeat cannot be part of any solution). Orbits of the anchor: 1 + 2 + 6x6 (probe a1); zero orbit w = 0; size-2 orbit (stabiliser <(16,pi)>) w in {0, 13, 26}; size-6 orbits w in Z39. Hence at most 1 + 3 + 6x39 = 238 options. The enumeration is exhaustive (all solutions counted).

runs.expect: >= 35 solutions incl. all constant rows (the deleted zero row and its translates)
>= 1 solution incl. the deleted zero row f = 0
exhaustive count; any solution = 7-row DM39 candidate -> STOP, pin, three checkers, parent

consequence: T1/T2 negative = only this anchor (with/without equivariance) has no one-row extension; no statement about other DM6 or about six MOLS(39). Positive = candidate.
